searchText: has anyone looked at making gastoken a part of the protocol? <@!332923501079953409> what would be the advantage of it being part of the protocol? EOAs could use the gas refunds directly without going through a proxy contract? <@332923501079953409> We don't actually want gas tokens, they aren't particularly healthy as they add for garbage to the chain with no benefits to the network itself. We can't stop them without getting rid of refunds though. > <@!332923501079953409> what would be the advantage of it being part of the protocol? EOAs could use the gas refunds directly without going through a proxy contract? <@!543900561460822016> Basically, yes. > <@!332923501079953409> We don't actually want gas tokens, they aren't particularly healthy as they add for age to the chain with no benefits to the network itself. <@!301186049323958275> "add age" what does this mean? I think gastoken is horrible for the chain, but what is being done to fix the issues? if we aren't going to remove the need for gastoken then we should make it first class, IMO. (typo) Yes, if it was in the protocol we could cleanup the garbage, is my shoot from the hip thinking. What we *want* is for people to move real transactions/load to off-peak, not for people to show up during off-peak and buy peak credits. The electricity company, for example, isn't going to let you pay for electricity in the middle of the night (at night prices) that is then delivered in the middle of the day (when they have shortages). That's true, and basically my point. we should probably make it easier for users to actually shift the load. I often have load that I wouldn't mind shifting to off peak, but gas price volatility is such that it is really hard to predict that. Also, if you don't have your own node, low price transactions get pushed from pending queue. Escalator gas pricing could help with this? Set an escalator that escalates slowly over 2 days, giving you high guarantee that you'll get in eventually, but let's you low-ball the gas price. yeah, i mean... this stuff is fairly predictable in terms of "foreseeable problems" and the tooling to fix this should really be done at the wallet level, but there are all sorts of problems there. It's actually kinda insane that The EF funded wallet development at one point and then stopped.
